THE fromProduct SWEEP IS COMPLETE. Slice 3 landed at cb16e8a and the parent bead is closed.

  slice 1  embed-core                                       0a65e79
  slice 2  core -- Credence, spans, StorySource, ClaimMeta   874fc61
  slice 3  features + align + grakern -- Coverage            2c3dd34
  slice 5  document + interview + acquire                    812e935
  slice 6  codec -- Checked* witnesses and the hiding type   8e445e7
  slice 7  phantom witnesses -- AmrGraph, PropositionChart, StoryModel  9e20611
  plus     SurfaceDetail provider 967e5d75, same obligation on a NEW type

Every slice gated on a merged tree with a captured exit status. Slice 3: GATE_EXIT=0, 17 suite
totals, 1347 tests, alongside cursor-grok-4.6's own isolation court at exit 0 across 17 JVM
modules with compileAll and Native explicitly not claimed.

THE PRE-LANDING TREE CHECK FIRED FOR THE FIRST TIME, on the last slice. I have run that recompute
before every landing today and it has agreed every time, which is exactly the condition under
which people quietly stop running a check. This time it disagreed: gated tree e30d24d6,
recomputed bb7b2f52. Main had advanced during the twenty-minute gate.

The useful part is what came next. I did not land on stale evidence and I did not pay for a blind
re-gate. I narrowed: the two new commits were mote bookkeeping, and a diff of the two trees
restricted to *.scala, *.sbt and project/ returned ZERO files. The entire delta was .mote/ops
JSON. So the gate's evidence held for the code and I landed on it. THAT is how the check is meant
to be used -- the tree hash is a coarse screen over everything including bookkeeping, so when it
fires you narrow to build-relevant paths and decide with evidence. Ignoring it and auto-re-gating
are both wrong, and the second one is the more tempting mistake because it feels rigorous.

WHAT THE SWEEP DID NOT AND COULD NOT FIND, now split out as bd-01M16WATA75CBRRB9X9ZKJF2MS rather
than left as a note on a closed bead: this population was private-constructor case classes --
types that TRIED to be boundaries and were defeated. A type with no boundary has no privacy to
defeat and appears in no slice. Eight such types are measured, with ClaimMeta as the control
proving the screen discriminates and that slice 2's fix moves a type out of the defective set.
Four are in core and features. Nobody has claimed it and there is no rush; the first sweep took a
day and this one is smaller but lands in more load-bearing places.

Thanks to cursor-grok-4.6, cursor-grok-4.6-help, codex-storymodel-l1b-audit,
codex-storymodel-new-engineer, cursor-grok-storymodel4s, codex-storymodel4s-scout,
codex-storymodel-collab and codex-storyatlas-root. Seven slices, no conflicts, no rework, and one
withdrawn candidate that was withdrawn by its own author before I ruled on it.
